transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (CTO - Acme Health), Elena García (Head of MLOps), Samir Patel (Security), Liam O'Connor (Product)

Summary (auto): quick intro, qualification, success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarking plan, timelines and next steps.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining. Marcus, thanks for organizing, do you want to kick off with a quick bit of context on what you're trying to achieve with this POC?
[00:12] Marcus: Yeah sure. Hi all, so Acme Health is building an internal clinical summarization feature, patient note summarization, and a realtime triage assistant. Primary needs are strict PHI handling, low latency for triage (we're aiming p95 under 200ms ideally), and predictable cost. We're evaluating whether hosted Redwood API will be acceptable or we need dedicated capacity or full private/on-prem.
[00:33] Elena: Right, and from infra perspective we need data residency in our US-east tenancy and we have FHIR payloads in S3. We can't send certain PHI fields offsite without a covered arrangement.
[00:45] Priya: thanks. Quick clarifying q: when you say p95 under 200ms, is that token-level latency or end-to-end request?
[00:52] Marcus: End-to-end, including network and our preprocessing. Our internal target for model inference is around 120ms p95 if possible. 
[01:03] Priya: got it. That helps a lot. For sizing, can you share typical sequence lengths and qps?
[01:08] Marcus: Average sequence 384 tokens, some up to 1k during long notes. Baseline traffic is about 1k requests/day, but we have burst patterns during morning rounds up to 400-500 qps for short periods. Concurrent requests around 150 sustained during peak windows.
[01:24] Samir: from security, we need assurance on encryption at rest for logs, KMS integration, SOC2 type II, audit trails, and optional dedicated HSM. Also SSO/SAML + RBAC.
[01:36] Jordan: Absolutely. Redwood supports KMS integrations, SOC2, SAML; we'll share our security pack. For dedicated and private we can discuss HSM options.
[01:45] Liam: Also curious about model versions and rollback; we need to pin model versions and run A/B rollouts during the pilot.
[01:52] Priya: That maps well to Redwood rollout features: can canary to a fraction of traffic and fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes. Note — I might say 'Redwood Dedicate' sometimes; sorry for the slip, it's Redwood Dedicated.
[02:05] Marcus: no worries. Can you talk through the high-level tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, Private for us?
[02:12] Jordan: Sure. Hosted: fastest to start, pay-as-you-go, Redwood manages everything. Tradeoff: multi-tenant environment means less control over exact hardware, though our hosted offering still has strong isolation and SOC2 controls. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for you, predictable throughput, custom autoscale, and better cost per token at scale. Private: VPC or on-prem — full control, best for strict data residency and compliance, but longer lead time to deploy and ops responsibility sits more with you.
[02:40] Elena: What kind of lead times for private?
[02:42] Priya: For a Private VPC deployment it's typically 4–6 weeks to stand up the control plane and connect networking; on-prem can be 8–12 weeks depending on procurement and hardware.
[02:52] Marcus: And Dedicated?
[02:54] Jordan: Dedicated allocation can usually be reserved and started in 1–2 weeks depending on capacity and region. Pricing will reflect reserved commit.
[03:02] Samir: what's the fallback during capacity constraints? Say if dedicated pool is saturated.
[03:07] Priya: We have smart routing and automatic fallback policies — traffic can be routed to a compatible model variant or to hosted pool as a failover. We also have configurable priorities so critical routes get first dibs.
[03:20] Marcus: On benchmarks — what would you run in an initial POC?
[03:23] Priya: We propose two stages: stage one hosted benchmark to validate latency and correctness with your sample workload; stage two dedicated sizing benchmark to determine required GPUs and autoscale policies. If data residency forces it, run private/on-prem bench after that.
[03:40] Liam: How long does each stage take?
[03:42] Priya: Hosted benchmark can be done in 3–5 business days once we have the sample dataset and traffic profile. Dedicated sizing is another 1–2 weeks for the sizing runs, and private deployment is longer as noted. Overall POC timeline commonly 4–6 weeks end-to-end for hosted->dedicated path.
[03:58] Marcus: Success criteria for us: 1) p95 inference latency under 150ms end-to-end on inference path, 2) quality: ROUGE/factuality regression within 2% of baseline on our eval set, 3) cost target less than $X per 1M tokens (we'll share target), 4) security: KMS, audit logs, and a contractual data residency guarantee.
[04:21] Jordan: we can map those. For quality we'll run your eval set; for latency we'll run synthetic and replay traffic with your payloads. For cost we'll provide model and quantization recommendations — e.g., quantized 4-bit runs reduce cost but we should validate quality.
[04:36] Marcus: any caveats on quantization for clinical text? We can't sacrifice hallucination rates.
[04:41] Priya: absolutely — quantization can slightly change model behavior. Our Optimize team recommends A/B tests and targeted evals; we'll include eval harness and regression alerts.
[04:52] Samir: about logs — can you redact PII before sending logs to Redwood hosted analytics? We can't have raw PHI in third-party logs.
[04:59] Jordan: yes, log redaction and filtered telemetry options exist; also dedicated/private gives more control to keep logs inside your VPC. We'll include config options.
[05:10] Elena: For the hosted benchmark, do you need full PHI data?
[05:13] Priya: no, we'd prefer a de-identified sample. If necessary we can run agent-side instrumentation so raw PHI never leaves your network and we still get metrics.
[05:23] Marcus: cool. For traffic patterns, we have daytime peaks 7–9am EST and nights are low. Bursts are short ~10–20 minutes.
[05:31] Priya: that'll affect batching and autoscale config — continuous batching helps throughput but can add latency; for low-latency triage we might prioritize lower batch size and more concurrency.
[05:41] Liam: is there a tuning knob for cost vs latency exposed?
[05:44] Jordan: yes — batching, caching (prefix/KV cache), quantization profiles and model selection. We'll provide recommendations based on the POC results.
[05:55] Marcus: on the decision criteria matrix, can you outline which factors push us to dedicated vs private?
[06:00] Priya: From experience: if data residency and full audit isolation is non-negotiable -> Private. If you need predictable throughput and significantly lower unit cost at scale but can accept some managed infra -> Dedicated. If speed to market and low ops footprint is priority and compliance can be handled contractually -> Hosted. Also consider procurement and budget timelines — dedicated and private require longer procurement cycles.
[06:23] Samir: procurement note — we need a BAA and vetted subprocessors list.
[06:27] Jordan: we'll include those in the security pack.
[06:30] Marcus: ok let's talk benchmarks specifics — what metrics and how we measure?
[06:34] Priya: Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, throughput (rps), failure/error rates, memory/kv cache hit rate, and model quality metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, custom factuality score). We'll run three load profiles: baseline (1k/day), peak burst (500qps), and sustained high (150 concurrent).
[06:56] Priya: We'll supply a benchmark harness (locally run) and a JMeter-like load generator. For hosted tests we run from Redwood infra against your dev key; for dedicated we spin up a reserved pool and run same tests.
[07:10] Marcus: do you maintain the test harness in a repo we can review?
[07:12] Priya: yes — we'll share a GitHub repo link and a runbook.
[07:16] Liam: what about regression alerts you mentioned? How are those triggered?
[07:20] Jordan: Redwood Optimize can monitor a set of eval prompts and surface drift or quality regressions; we set thresholds and can integrate with Slack/email for alerts.
[07:29] Marcus: good. Any notable limitations we should be aware of in hosted mode for PHI?
[07:33] Priya: hosted is SOC2 and we have contractual controls, but if your legal requires no third-party access to plaintext PHI or on-prem-only storage, then you'll need Private. Hosted offers strong isolation but not full on-premairgapped scenarios.
[07:47] Samir: noted. For private on-prem, is there a preferred hardware spec?
[07:51] Priya: we provide recommended GPU SKUs (A100 or H100 depending on model), minimum NVMe for KV caches, and network requirements; we'll share a hardware guide.
[07:59] Jordan: ok, let's align on immediate next steps for the POC. Proposal: 1) Acme to provide de-identified sample dataset and traffic profile by 2026-03-03. 2) Redwood to run hosted benchmark within 3 business days of receiving data and share results. 3) If hosted shows latency or cost issues, proceed to dedicated sizing run (1–2 weeks). 4) In parallel, schedule private deep dive if legal requires it.
[08:28] Marcus: that timeline looks good. On procurement, we'll start internal approvals but need the pricing sheet to estimate cost.
[08:34] Jordan: I'll send hosted and dedicated pricing tiers and an estimated cost model.
[08:38] Priya: And I'll share the benchmark repo, runbook, and an evaluation checklist — includes quality tests you'll want to run.
[08:45] Liam: Can you include sample dashboards for latency and token cost?
[08:48] Jordan: yes, we'll share screenshots from Redwood Console and an example cost break down per route/model.
[08:52] Samir: last question — any known vendor lock-in risks? If we start with hosted then move to private, how hard is migration?
[08:59] Priya: We design for portability: same API and model/versioning across deployments. There are infra differences but export/import for models and KV cache state is supported; migration work mainly around networking and user access. We'll include a migration checklist.
[09:12] Marcus: perfect. I think that's enough to move forward. Thanks everyone.
[09:16] Jordan: thanks — quick recap: Jordan send pricing and security pack; Priya send benchmark repo and runbook; Marcus provide sample dataset and traffic profile. We'll meet again after initial hosted benchmark to review results.
[09:29] Elena: thanks all, talk soon.
[09:31] End meeting.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors: 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated', 'A hundred' vs 'H100' sometimes mistranscribed, names occasionally misspelled (common in automated transcripts).
